Demolition Begins On Popular Villanova Off-Campus College Hall Apartments

Dylan Johnson, Co-Editor-in-Chief
August 21, 2026
Courtesy of Michael Johnson
College Hall, colloquially known as “Courts” to Villanova students, was demolished this week.
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:41
Instaread

On Tuesday, Aug. 19, the demolition process began on College Hall in Bryn Mawr, PA, a longtime off-campus apartment complex for generations of Villanova students.

The apartment complex, which was colloquially known as “Courts”, was a popular party spot for Villanova students for the last several decades and is being demolished after the Shipley School acquired the 17-acre property for $12 million in August 2025. 

In 2024, College Hall came under pressure from Lower Merion Township and the Lower Merion Police after a large number of complaints poured in from locals who lived in the surrounding area of the apartment complex. At the time, around 100 Villanova students were living in the apartment complex.

In The Villanovan’s 2024 report, police reports from the first two weeks of the Fall 2022 semester indicated that the Lower Merion Police Department (LMPD) received just three complaint calls from community members related to College Hall. However, a year later in 2023, during the same period, the LMPD received 10 complaints about the 800 block of Montgomery Avenue, where College Hall is located.

These complaints included rowdy behavior, noisy parties, underage drinking and fire alarm activation. 

Community complaints eventually forced Altman Management Co., the owner of College Hall, to sell the property to the adjacent Shipley School last year. 

The Shipley School, a pre-K through 12 co-ed independent school, had been in talks about acquiring the complex “for decades,” according to its Head of School, Ian Craig, in a message to the school community in August 2025. 

“We are currently engaged in a Campus Planning process with outside architects to determine the long-term use of the property,” Craig wrote in an email to The Villanovan.

About the Contributor
Dylan Johnson, Co-Editor-in-Chief
Dylan Johnson has recently taken over one of the two Co-Editor-in-Chief roles for 2026. He is currently pursuing a major in Communications with a specialization in journalism. Dylan is a junior from Philadelphia, PA. Dylan’s passion for journalism is driven by storytelling. At The Villanovan, he wants to discover and tell the stories that might otherwise go untold. Outside of the paper, Dylan is currently working for The Philadelphia Inquirer as a Sports Intern. Dylan is a hard worker who is always looking for the next article to write. He is a diehard Philadelphia sports fan and will never miss an Eagles game. He can always be found at a Villanova game, whether it be in a press box, on the sidelines, or in the stands. When he is not spending hours in the Finn’s media room, Dylan can be found enjoying runs around campus.
